summary: Defines a set of Cryptographic Message Syntax content types that hold CBOR content, allowing CBOR data to be signed, encrypted or otherwise protected using CMS.

subtitle: Registers content types to wrap compact binary objects in cryptographic containers.

tldr.problem: CBOR (Concise Binary Object Representation) is a compact data format widely used in constrained environments, but there was no standard way to protect CBOR content using CMS (Cryptographic Message Syntax), which is the common method for signing and encrypting messages.
tldr.mechanism: This RFC defines two new CMS content type identifiers: one for a single CBOR object and one for a sequence of CBOR objects concatenated together, allowing CBOR data to be wrapped in CMS security containers without misidentifying it as generic data.
tldr.outcome: Applications can now clearly label and protect CBOR content using existing CMS infrastructure, with registered object identifiers and MIME type parameters for both single and sequence formats.

today: RFC 8769 is an Informational RFC published in March 2020 and has not been obsoleted. The registered content types are part of the IANA SMI registry and can be used by any application that needs to protect CBOR data using CMS.

sections.title: Introduction
sections.content:
CBOR (Concise Binary Object Representation) is a compact self-describing binary encoding now widely used in applications, especially in Internet of Things and constrained environments where small data size is crucial. CMS (Cryptographic Message Syntax) is the standard method for applying signatures, encryption, and other security protections to messages. When CBOR content is protected using CMS, there was no standard way to identify that the content inside was CBOR rather than generic binary data.

This RFC addresses that gap by registering two new content type identifiers for CMS. These identifiers allow implementations to clearly label CBOR objects and CBOR sequences when wrapping them with CMS security containers, making it possible for applications to handle them correctly without ambiguity.
sections.plainLanguage: When you put something in a locked box, you write a label saying what is inside. This document defines the labels for putting CBOR in a CMS security box.

sections.title: CBOR Content Types
sections.content:
The RFC defines two content types. The CBOR content type (id-ct-cbor) refers to a single encoded CBOR item of any kind; CBOR's self-describing format allows decoders to reconstruct the structure without additional metadata. The CBOR Sequence content type (id-ct-cborSequence) refers to a sequence of zero or more CBOR objects concatenated one after another without delimiters between them.

Both content types are intended for use with CMS signed-data and authenticated-enveloped-data structures, though they can be included in any CMS wrapper. The RFC also defines how these content types should appear in HTTP content-type headers using the innerContent parameter introduced by RFC 7193.
sections.plainLanguage: One type is for a single compact package, the other is for a row of packages stacked together. Both types go inside CMS security containers.

sections.title: Security and Registration
sections.content:
The content type registration itself introduces no new security issues; it is purely a labeling mechanism. By using distinct object identifiers instead of the generic data identifier, the document reduces confusion and makes it less likely that CBOR content will be mishandled by applications expecting a different format.

IANA has registered the object identifiers for both content types and the corresponding MIME type parameter values (cbor and cborSequence), allowing applications to reliably detect and correctly process CBOR protected by CMS.
sections.plainLanguage: Giving things clear names keeps them safe from being mixed up. These registrations are how the internet remembers what goes in each kind of box.

sections.title: Implementation Details
sections.content:
The RFC includes an ASN.1 module defining the syntax for the new content types in a form that implementers can reference. The module imports the CONTENT-TYPE framework from the CMS standard specification and defines the object identifiers and their corresponding CONTENT-TYPE entries.

The object identifier for CBOR content is 1.2.840.113549.1.9.16.1.44, and for CBOR Sequence it is 1.2.840.113549.1.9.16.1.45. These are registered in the SMI registry maintained by IANA.
sections.plainLanguage: Computers need exact numbers to identify things reliably. These are the official numbers for CBOR and CBOR Sequence in the security system.
